lines.trans: I found your little elephant here.
Where? It was in the restaurant, right? I knew it.
Thank you so much. You can't imagine how dear this thing is to me.
Don't mention it, Dad. Try not to lose what is dear to you anymore.
Sometimes we try long and hard to find the key to unlock a door.
But in the end we realize that the right key was never on the keyring.
Something that we will never know about.
Although we understand that it is the door to the future.
To the future in which we would like to find ourselves.
If you open the wrong door, someone else will open yours.
Viktoria, it seems to me...
It seems that I love you.

examples.trans: Nobody irritates cooks more than waiters.

examples.text: Они бесцеремонны.
examples.trans: They are unceremonious.

examples.text: Моя камбала там не постарела, а?
examples.trans: Hasn't my flounder grown old over there, huh?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will find out, know', paired with 'узнавать'.

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, а позвольте узнать повод?
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, may I ask the occasion?

examples.text: То, о чём мы никогда не узнаем.
examples.trans: Something that we will never know about.

examples.text: Ты меня узнал?
examples.trans: Did you recognise me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Хотел тебя предупредить, мы завтра идём в кино.
examples.trans: I wanted to let you know, tomorrow we are going to the cinema.

examples.text: Вика, я хотел с тобой поговорить.
examples.trans: Vika, I wanted to talk with you.

examples.text: Я просто хотел сказать, что мне вчера показалось...
examples.trans: I just wanted to say that yesterday it seemed to me...

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф, это не ерунда, это большая игра.
examples.trans: Chef, this is not nonsense, this is a big game.

examples.text: Это большая игра!
examples.trans: This is a big game!

examples.text: И это солидные деньги? Марш работать!
examples.trans: And that is serious money? March back to work!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('future, next').

examples.text: Хотя понимаем, что это дверь в будущее.
examples.trans: Although we understand that it is the door to the future.

examples.text: В то будущее, в котором нам бы хотелось оказаться.
examples.trans: To the future in which we would like to find ourselves.

examples.text: Это будущий мэр Синеозерска!
examples.trans: That is the future mayor of Sineozersk!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who, which (relative)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Небрежный. Хуже только официант, который был поваром.
examples.trans: Careless. Worse is only a waiter who used to be a cook.

examples.text: А почему ты слоника не носишь, который я тебе подарила?
examples.trans: And why aren't you carrying the little elephant that I gave you?

examples.text: Твоя задача какая? Следить за едой, которую ты мне подаёшь.
examples.trans: What is your job? To watch over the food that you serve me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Федя, ты можешь побыстрее?
examples.trans: Fedya, can you go faster?

examples.text: Нетерпеливый! Девушки просят меня быть помедленнее.
examples.trans: Impatient! Girls ask me to go more slowly.

examples.text: Давай быстрее готовь!
examples.trans: Come on, cook faster!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to feel like, to want (impersonal)', paired with 'захотеться'.

examples.text: Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: I understand you really want the flat.

examples.text: Мне очень хочется спать.
examples.trans: I really feel like sleeping.

examples.text: Самсоновы, ну вы очнитесь! Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: Samsonovs, come to your senses! I understand you really want the flat.

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find oneself, end up', paired with 'оказываться'.

examples.text: В то будущее, в котором нам бы хотелось оказаться.
examples.trans: To the future in which we would like to find ourselves.

examples.text: Ты оказалась неблагодарной.
examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.
examples.trans: He suddenly found himself in the center of events.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если честно, не очень.
examples.trans: To be honest, not really.

examples.text: Если вы откроете не ту дверь, вашу откроет кто-то другой.
examples.trans: If you open the wrong door, someone else will open yours.

examples.text: Если хочешь, приходи.
examples.trans: Come if you want.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нетерпеливый! Девушки просят меня быть помедленнее.
examples.trans: Impatient! Girls ask me to go more slowly.

examples.text: А я виноват, что вы такие криворукие?
examples.trans: Am I to blame that you are so clumsy?

examples.text: Крылья, говорит, прямо вырастают.
examples.trans: Wings, he says, sprout right out.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'open', paired with 'открывать'.

examples.text: Открытый чемпионат кухни по сбиванию банок. Солидные деньги на кону.
examples.trans: The open kitchen can-knocking championship. Serious money is at stake.

examples.text: Откройте дверь.
examples.trans: Open the door.

examples.text: Открой окно.
examples.trans: Open the window.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А это как раз тот самый холодец, который я собирался вам принести.
examples.trans: And this is that very aspic that I was going to bring you.

examples.text: Лена, ну не ты виновата, а слон этот, которого я потерял!
examples.trans: Lena, well you aren't to blame, it's that elephant that I lost!

examples.text: Это то, что ты говорил.
examples.trans: That's what you said.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне стыдно ваше блюдо в зал нести.
examples.trans: I am ashamed to carry your dish into the dining room.

examples.text: Клянусь, я не знаю, где ваш слон.
examples.trans: I swear, I don't know where your elephant is.

examples.text: Если вы откроете не ту дверь, вашу откроет кто-то другой.
examples.trans: If you open the wrong door, someone else will open yours.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Умер кто-то? Нет.
examples.trans: Did someone die? No.

examples.text: Если вы откроете не ту дверь, вашу откроет кто-то другой.
examples.trans: If you open the wrong door, someone else will open yours.

examples.text: Наконец-то кто-то за народ!
examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('another').

examples.text: Ну, что делать? Другой раз, так другой раз.
examples.trans: Well, what can we do? Another time, then another time.

examples.text: Я вдруг осознал, что ты — это всё, что мне нужно.
examples.trans: I suddenly realized that you are everything I need.

examples.text: Если вы откроете не ту дверь, вашу откроет кто-то другой.
examples.trans: If you open the wrong door, someone else will open yours.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'it seems', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.text: Я просто хотел сказать, что мне вчера показалось...
examples.trans: I just wanted to say that yesterday it seemed to me...

examples.text: То есть вы хотите сказать...
examples.trans: So you mean to say...

examples.text: В то будущее, в котором нам бы хотелось оказаться.
examples.trans: To the future in which we would like to find ourselves.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город.
examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Ты любишь жвачку?
examples.trans: Do you like gum?

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
